To compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a Wireless Communication competitor without unsupported claims, we need direct, cited evidence that connects the R&S product, the competitor product, and the specific wireless test requirement being compared; separate co-mentions are not enough [68].
Claims such as “only,” “industry’s only,” “fully integrated,” “long-term scalability,” or “lower TCO” require verification in formal datasheets, features documents, conformance reports, or configuration tools before use [1].  
For R&S CMX500 signaling claims, the formal sources are the CMX500 Specifications Version 11.00 and CMX500 Features and Functions Version 32 / CSW 9.20.0 and higher [9].  
For CMX500, the Specifications document is binding only under its stated operating, calibration, adjustment, and environmental conditions [9].  
For CMX500, the Features and Functions document is a feature overview, and data without tolerance limits is not binding [9].  
For R&S CMX500 signaling capability, supported evidence includes LTE, NR FR1, NR FR2, NSA, SA, FDD, TDD, WLAN signaling, WLAN TX measurements, fading, AWGN, BLER, throughput measurement, application testing, IP traffic analysis, IMS/audio/POLQA, GUI, graphical scripting, XLAPI, and SCPI remote control [6].  
For R&S CMP180 non-signaling / production wireless communication testing, supported evidence includes that it is a Radio Communication Tester for production / wireless communication device testing with configurable RF generator/analyzer, communication-standard measurement options, waveform options, and R&S VSE analysis capability [38].  
For CMP180, supported evidence also includes simultaneous receiver and transmitter testing and a multiport RF architecture with RF generator/analyzer no. 1 and optional no. 2 [39].  
For our configuration or option claims, formal configuration evidence is required because the Signaling test solution note does not identify a formal configuration guide, software version, license bundle, quote-tool version, or release date [23].  
The Signaling test solution source should not replace official specifications or a configuration tool [24].  
For competitor claims about Keysight UXM, official Keysight datasheets, feature documents, order data, or service terms are required because the current wireless UXM information comes from an R&S battle card and is not Keysight official data [36].  
For competitor claims about Anritsu, official Anritsu documents and third-party evidence are required before using battle-card claims in customer documents [54].  
For competitor claims about Amarisoft, the battle-card information is only an R&S sales viewpoint and does not cite Amarisoft official documents [55].  
Any claim about TCO, fewer boxes, higher throughput, market leadership, or “only platform” requires independent evidence because those phrases are identified as sales language rather than verifiable technical specifications [54].  
For throughput, bandwidth, FR3, RFU18, roadmap, or “verified” performance claims, evidence must include formal specifications or reports with setup, DUT, band combination, software release, and test conditions, because the available callbox source does not provide those details for such claims [18].

2026_02_CMX500_Keysight_Sales_Battle_Card › Battle card 中的 R&S positioning
來源的 positioning statement 主張：

- [[Rohde & Schwarz]] delivers the industry’s only fully integrated platform for FR1、FR2、Wi-Fi、fading、IP throughput、RF analysis、NTN、RedCap and end-to-end signalling in one instrument。
- 來源說 [[Keysight]] spreads equivalent capabilities across multiple UXM models、add-on software and external tools。
- 來源說 R&S ensures long-term scalability、measurement accuracy and path from R&D to certification without hardware fragmentation。

使用限制：以上是 sales language；其中 only、industry’s only、fully integrated、long-term scalability、lower TCO 等敘述不能當作可驗證規格，需回查正式 datasheet、features document、conformance report 或配置工具。

2026_02_CMX500_Keysight_Sales_Battle_Card › 重點摘要
- 來源將 [[Keysight]] 描述為大型美國 test & measurement vendor，總部在 Santa Rosa, California, USA，員工數約 **16,800+**，在 semiconductor、aerospace / defense、cloud 與 wireless testing 具有強市場存在。
- 來源主張 [[Keysight]] mobile communications strategy 越來越 software-led 與 AI-driven，但 [[Keysight UXM]] portfolio 分散於多個 hardware SKUs：[[Keysight E7515P]]、[[Keysight E7515W]]、[[Keysight E7515B]]、[[Keysight E7515E]]、[[Keysight E7515R]]。
- 來源列出 [[Keysight]] portfolio 包含 UXM 5G Wireless Test Platforms、[[ProbSim]] channel emulators、[[Nemo]] field test tools、[[RaySim]] digital twin engine、[[Atlas]] AI-powered device test、C-V2X 與 cybersecurity tools。
- 來源把 R&S positioning 表述為：[[R&S CMX500]] 在 one instrument 中整合 [[NR FR1]]、[[NR FR2]]、[[Wi-Fi]]、[[Fading]]、IP throughput、RF analysis、[[NTN]]、[[RedCap]] 與 end-to-end signaling；而 Keysight 需分散於多個 UXM models、add-on software 與 external tools。
- 來源主張 [[R&S CMX500]] 的差異化包含 one-platform architecture、integrated fading + IP + application testing、unified software ecosystem（[[CMsquares]]、[[R&S CMsequencer]]、AI Script Assistant）、measurement leadership、FR3 / 6G path、cellular + Wi-Fi in one platform，以及 NTN / RedCap / operator certification leadership。
- 來源對 [[Keysight]] 的弱點敘述包含 hardware fragmentation、multi-tool workflow、advanced testing external dependencies、limited legacy、Wi-Fi only on selected models、FR3 / 6G roadmap relies on add-ons。
- 來源的 quick comparison table 將 R&S / CMX500 描述為 one platform：FR1 + FR2 + FR3 + WLAN + fading + IP + NTN + LTE + RedCap；將 Keysight 描述為 multiple UXM SKUs + external tools。

To compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a Wireless Communication competitor without unsupported claims, we need direct, cited evidence that connects the R&S product, the competitor product, and the specific wireless test requirement being compared; separate co-mentions are not enough [68].
Claims such as “only,” “industry’s only,” “fully integrated,” “long-term scalability,” or “lower TCO” require verification in formal datasheets, features documents, conformance reports, or configuration tools before use [1].  
For R&S CMX500 signaling claims, the formal sources are the CMX500 Specifications Version 11.00 and CMX500 Features and Functions Version 32 / CSW 9.20.0 and higher [9].  
For CMX500, the Specifications document is binding only under its stated operating, calibration, adjustment, and environmental conditions [9].  
For CMX500, the Features and Functions document is a feature overview, and data without tolerance limits is not binding [9].  
For R&S CMX500 signaling capability, supported evidence includes LTE, NR FR1, NR FR2, NSA, SA, FDD, TDD, WLAN signaling, WLAN TX measurements, fading, AWGN, BLER, throughput measurement, application testing, IP traffic analysis, IMS/audio/POLQA, GUI, graphical scripting, XLAPI, and SCPI remote control [6].  
For R&S CMP180 non-signaling / production wireless communication testing, supported evidence includes that it is a Radio Communication Tester for production / wireless communication device testing with configurable RF generator/analyzer, communication-standard measurement options, waveform options, and R&S VSE analysis capability [38].  
For CMP180, supported evidence also includes simultaneous receiver and transmitter testing and a multiport RF architecture with RF generator/analyzer no. 1 and optional no. 2 [39].  
For our configuration or option claims, formal configuration evidence is required because the Signaling test solution note does not identify a formal configuration guide, software version, license bundle, quote-tool version, or release date [23].  
The Signaling test solution source should not replace official specifications or a configuration tool [24].  
For competitor claims about Keysight UXM, official Keysight datasheets, feature documents, order data, or service terms are required because the current wireless UXM information comes from an R&S battle card and is not Keysight official data [36].  
For competitor claims about Anritsu, official Anritsu documents and third-party evidence are required before using battle-card claims in customer documents [54].  
For competitor claims about Amarisoft, the battle-card information is only an R&S sales viewpoint and does not cite Amarisoft official documents [55].  
Any claim about TCO, fewer boxes, higher throughput, market leadership, or “only platform” requires independent evidence because those phrases are identified as sales language rather than verifiable technical specifications [54].  
For throughput, bandwidth, FR3, RFU18, roadmap, or “verified” performance claims, evidence must include formal specifications or reports with setup, DUT, band combination, software release, and test conditions, because the available callbox source does not provide those details for such claims [18].
